QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_14

question.text: Rohit was allotted share warrants of a listed company at Rs.50 per warrant, paying 25% upfront (Rs.12.50 per warrant). He exercised the warrants within 18 months by paying the balance Rs.37.50 per warrant, converting them into equity shares when the fair market value of the shares at conversion was Rs.50 per share. He later sold the listed shares (with STT paid) at Rs.80 per share after holding them for 14 months from the date of conversion. For the subsequent sale of shares (ignoring the separate warrant-conversion event since FMV equals strike), what is his cost of acquisition per share and the nature and rate of gain on the share sale?

answer.text: Cost Rs.37.50; LTCG of Rs.42.50 per share at 12.5%
Cost Rs.50; LTCG of Rs.30 per share at 12.5% under Section 112A
Cost Rs.50; STCG of Rs.30 per share at 20% under Section 111A
Cost Rs.12.50; LTCG of Rs.67.50 per share at 12.5%

explanation.text: The Logic: The cost of acquisition of the resulting shares equals the FMV on the date of conversion under the source mechanics; here that FMV is Rs.50, equal to the total of the upfront warrant payment (Rs.12.50) plus the exercise price (Rs.37.50). The holding period for the resulting listed equity shares begins from the date of conversion. Rohit sold after 14 months from conversion, which exceeds 12 months, so the gain is LTCG. With STT paid on a listed equity share, LTCG is taxed at 12.5% under Section 112A. Gain per share = Rs.80 - Rs.50 = Rs.30. The Trap: Option A uses only the exercise price (Rs.37.50) as cost. Option D uses only the upfront payment (Rs.12.50) as cost. Option C correctly identifies Rs.50 cost but misclassifies a 14-month holding as STCG. Note: NISM Series X-B workbook (pages 237-240) supports treating conversion of listed share warrants as a taxable transfer of the warrants (gain = FMV of shares on conversion less strike); here FMV equals strike, so the warrant-conversion gain is nil. The later share sale follows ordinary listed-equity LTCG rules under Section 112A.
